## ➕ A fourth site of this card's mechanism, and one more path that reaches site 1 — measured while closing objectui#10110

`domain:ui` seat #1, `session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`. Source: the objectui#10110 measurement report `5808905560`, driven through the console's own route components in `America/Los_Angeles` and `UTC` on `origin/main` `62597c5`, with a datetime control that rendered different calendar days in the two zones (so the zone really moved). ⛔ No card is filed for these: this card already owns the mechanism, and its body calls the three sites 「a floor rather than a census」.

### Site 4 — `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` · `DateCellRenderer`, the overdue colouring

The TEXT is right (it hands the raw string to the repaired `formatDate`), but `isOverdueInstant(date, dueLike)` is fed `new Date(safe)` — UTC midnight — and compares it with the LOCAL start of day. Measured: a due-type `2026-09-03` on clock `2026-09-03T10:35Z` reads 「Today」 in both zones, **red** (`text-red-600`) west of UTC and not red in UTC. That held in all four list cases. This seat re-read the code on `main`: the comment above that line still says `new Date(safe)` 「reproduces `formatDate`'s own parse exactly」, which stopped being true when PR objectui#10182 moved `formatDate` onto `toDisplayDate`. ⚠️ Not probed in the other placements the same renderer draws (`DetailSection`, `HeaderHighlight`, `RelatedList`).

⚠️ For whoever takes this card: the dev reported that a repair through the shared path needs the module-private `toDisplayDate` exposed from `@object-ui/core`. That is a new export, so the claim will have to weigh `Clause-②`. The other route, a local re-parse, re-creates the two conventions objectui#10182 removed.

### Another path into site 1 (`data-table.tsx` · `formatCellValue`)

`RelatedList` cells fall back to `data-table`'s `formatCellValue` whenever the child object's schema is unavailable: an adapter without `getObjectSchema`, or a rejected schema read, with `relatedListColumns` declared. West of UTC they then shift: `2026-09-01` / `10-01` / `11-01` → 「Aug 31」/「Sep 30」/「Oct 31」 (LA) against 「Sep 1」/「Oct 1」/「Nov 1」 (UTC). The site-1 repair covers it; its pin can include this path.

### A rig trap for this card's zone pin

The root `vitest.config.mts` sets `process.env.TZ = 'UTC'` in module scope, and resolving the project configs re-runs that line. So even a wrapper config that sets `TZ` in its own module scope reads `UTC` inside the workers (measured). What works: the child-process pin already in `date-display.dateOnlyZone-10110.test.ts`, or a `globalSetup` re-pin plus `--pool=forks`.
